title: Camping (official): campfire holds 3 features, 1 h shared cooldown, 1 min sit/craft for benefits, features from skill 20
claim: Blizzard's Oct 21 camping article: a Basic Campfire (Cooking 1) makes a shared campsite holding up to 3 more camp features (one per contributing player; upgraded Cooking campfires hold 5 or 10); features need a nearby campfire and share a 1-hour cooldown; sitting or crafting at the camp for at least 1 minute grants the other features' benefits; the first feature for each profession unlocks at skill 20.
detail: Feature list (values scale with level): First Aid Kit +3-56 Stamina (excl. Fortitude); Fishing Bowl +8% stats (excl. Kings); Alchemy Mana Well 10-29 mp5 (excl. Wisdom); Blacksmithing Sharpening Wheel +6-34 Strength for 1 h (excl. Strength of Earth); Enchanted Lute +28-260 armor, +0-13 stats, +0-22 resists (excl. Mark of the Wild); Engineering Reagent Bot (buy reagents); Herbalism Incense Candle +2-25 Intellect (excl. Arcane Intellect); Leatherworking Camp Tent rested XP up to 5% of a level (no effect if you already have more); Skinning Camp Chair +2% crit (excl. Moonkin Aura); Tailoring Faction Banner +14-32 Spirit (excl. Divine Spirit). Camp buffs are exclusive with the matching class buffs. Items needing skill 140+ drop in dungeons/raids. Mining has no listed feature. For leveling: one player per feature, so a solo leveler gets campfire + own profession feature; grouping at a camp stacks buffs. On PvP rulesets enemies can find your camp. Confirms n:20261010-camp-tent-rested-5pct and the 1 min rule in n:20261008-campfire-rules.

title: Camp Tent tops rested XP up to 5% of a level, once per hour
claim: Client data: Camp Tent (spell 1307230) lets you and others sitting nearby raise Rested XP to 5% of a level, with no effect if you already have more; it needs a Campfire nearby, triggers after 30 s of resting (1229487), and Boosted Rest (1229451) blocks another tent gain for 1 h.
detail: Now official: Blizzard's Oct 21 camping article says the Leatherworking Camp Tent (skill 20) 'increases Rested experience by 5% of a level' with no effect if rested already exceeds that, and all camp features share a 1 h cooldown (n:20261022-camp-features-official). Confirmed unchanged in builds 70425 and 70450 by a second client-data extract (forever-ref). So a tent is a small top-up (5% of a level per hour), not a big rested source; Well Rested (n:20261009-legacy-perk-numbers) raises rested gain and cap by 20%. Sewing Machine and Tanning Rack give all Camp Tent benefits. (70425 removed the Tent line from the 'Camp Benefits' summary aura's text only.) Blizzard says 1 min sitting or crafting at the camp grants the benefits; the client trigger is 30 s.

title: Beta client build 70532 (after the stress test): no game-data changes
claim: The beta came back around 01:49 UTC Oct 22 after the stress test with a forced client update; Daybreak Forever lists it as 1.60.1.70532 with 0 rows added, removed or changed versus 70450 in the spell, talent, quest, creature and item tables.
detail: Zorbrix (Blizzard) said the return hit 'a small snag' and told players to fully exit the Battle.net app to force the update. No patch notes; players asking for them got no answer. So leveling data (quest XP, spells, talents) is as in 70450 plus server-side hotfixes (e.g. the Oct 20 Mage hotfix). forever-ref has no 70532 snapshot yet. The beta closes Oct 23 10:00 PDT.

title: Legacy perks that cut downtime: Thrill of Adventure 1-5% HP/mana per kill, Quick and the Dead, Field Medicine
claim: Thrill of Adventure (Adventure, 5 ranks) restores 1/2/3/4/5% of max health and mana over 10 s after each killing blow on a non-trivial enemy (not in dungeons, raids or battlegrounds); The Quick and the Dead (2 ranks) gives +5/10% speed while dead and free helpful spells for 1/2 min after resurrection or until combat; Field Medicine (2 ranks) cuts Recently Bandaged by 5/10 s (not in instances).
detail: Beta characters (and stress-test characters) get 16 Legacy points, so a 5-rank Thrill of Adventure is affordable at launch only if you've earned points; at launch new accounts start with what they earn (Legacy opens at 25 per wowforeverguides). Forum testers on the beta call the kill-heal a big drop in eating/drinking for melee (one claims Warrior leveling feels trivial); one report says the HP bar filled more than 5%. Permanence (2 ranks) makes camp rest benefits and long class buffs last 50/100% longer; Well Rested speeds rested gain and raises the cap 4-20% (n:20261009-legacy-perk-numbers). Rank costs are not published.

title: Quest XP seen in game differs from the files for four starter quests
claim: ForeverDB's 'Changes seen in game' (one player report each, not confirmed): Follow That Kobold! (91758) 180 -> 35 XP, Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds (91772) 270 -> 360, Legging It (96821) 410 -> 550, Bloodtalon Matriarch (97223) 700 -> 775; the last three also pay no money in game.
detail: The left values match Glide's seed (fg_quests: 180, 270, 405, 700), so the knowledge base has the file values. Northshire (91758, 91772, level 4) and Durotar (96821 level 6, 97223 level 8). Looks like server-side XP retuning moved XP between steps of the Northshire kobold chain. Reported Oct 16-17 on build 70425/70450. Treat as reported until a second observation; Glide's own quest-turn-in logs could confirm.

title: Flight paths fly about 30 yd/s: flight time = path length / 30
claim: LibTaxiTime computes Forever flight times from the client's flight-path tables at 30 yards per second; against InFlight's measured Classic times this gives 29.96 yd/s median over 266 routes (SD 0.16), multi-stop routes are the sum of their hops, and Frequent Flier makes flights 20% faster.
detail: Routes.lua (generated by Tools/taxi_routes.py from the client tables) holds the path lengths, so it can give every Forever route including new ones (Riverglades, Gilneas, Dalaran). Calibration uses Classic timings, not Forever measurements; the addon replaces the prediction with your own landed time. Useful for Glide's flight-time model and for new routes the seed lacks.

title: Dun Morogh deathskip: die inside Coldridge Valley or you revive at Kharanos
claim: RestedXP's Forever guide now warns Gnome Warlocks doing the starting-zone deathskip to make sure the subzone shows Coldridge Valley when they die, otherwise they are sent to the Kharanos graveyard.
detail: Added Oct 22 (RXPGuides commit 3fcc7e67). Applies to any Dun Morogh starter using a deathskip. Res sickness only applies from level 10, so early deathskips are free apart from durability.
